meta.name: workflow_operating_instructions
meta.purpose: Full operating memory for SRT segmentation, image generation, video animation, mixed montage assembly, and known constraints.

global_principles.primary_rule: Always derive the visual pipeline from the real audio timing, not from a rewritten literary script.
global_principles.timing_rule: First create SRT from the real audio. Only after that generate prompts and build the shot plan.
global_principles.narrative_rule: Every shot, transition, and inserted visual must justify its place in the story, not merely look impressive in isolation.
global_principles.consistency_rule: Keep visual continuity by using stable character references and by preserving shot order from the timeline.
global_principles.source_of_truth_rule: For montage and automation, treat timeline/manifest files as the source of truth, not ad hoc folder inspection.
global_principles.mixed_cut_rule: If a video exists for a shot and the current cut strategy says that shot should be animated, use the video. Otherwise use the still image for that shot.

critical_pipeline_error.problem: The pipeline previously used one sentence = one prompt = one frame.
critical_pipeline_error.why_it_failed: Some SRT sentences were 10-18 seconds long, which produced overlong static holds in the montage.
critical_pipeline_error.correct_fix: Detect all segments longer than 5 seconds, split them into multiple shots before image generation, then rebuild the timeline.

veo_scene_planning_error.problem: A technically valid generator-ready package can still be wrong for VEO mixed-cut if it mirrors subtitle granularity too literally.
veo_scene_planning_error.why_it_failed: Very short SRT beats created too many scenes, repeated prompts, weak shot variation, and poor fit for 4s/6s/8s video generation.
veo_scene_planning_error.correct_fix: For VEO-first mixed-cut work, merge neighboring short SRT beats when meaning is preserved, target durations that map cleanly to 4s, 6s, or 8s generation, and avoid prompt duplication across adjacent scenes.

render_error_learned.problem: Mixed source image resolutions caused render freezes that looked like repeated frames.
render_error_learned.correct_fix: Normalize images to a single target resolution before slideshow assembly.

log_error_learned.problem: run_summary.json was treated like historical truth, but it is overwritten by each run.
log_error_learned.correct_fix: Use failed.jsonl and success.jsonl as authoritative append-only logs. Treat run_summary.json only as the latest single-run snapshot.

policy: Use the real audio/SRT text as the base for prompt timing.
Split long timed segments so no still frame is held longer than 5 seconds.
The shot plan must be computed before generating the final production set of images.
For VEO mixed-cut projects, do not preserve subtitle-level fragmentation by default; merge adjacent short SRT beats when one larger scene communicates the idea more cleanly.
For VEO mixed-cut projects, prefer scene durations that can map directly to 4s, 6s, or 8s generation presets.

prompt_generation_rules.style: Realistic, cinematic, suitable for video generation and still generation.
format_history: Prompt lines were converted to generator-friendly format so each paragraph is one prompt block.
Reference directives were moved inline to avoid paragraph split issues in external generators.
important_rules: Do not attach all character references to every prompt.
Attach only the references actually needed for that shot.
If a shot has no recurring character, use no character reference.
If a prompt generator splits on blank lines, the reference directive must stay in the same paragraph as the prompt.
For multilingual source scripts, keep `voice_text` in the source language if useful for auditability, but keep generator prompts themselves fully in English.
Do not include mixed-language `Scene beat` fragments inside final generator prompts when a clean English visual instruction can express the same idea.
For silent B-roll workflows, prompts must explicitly forbid generated narration, dialogue, lip-sync, talking heads, captions, and subtitle overlays.

veo_mixed_cut_authoring_rules.purpose: Rules for planning generator-ready mixed-cut scenes for VEO-style production under a separate external voice-over track.
rules: Optimize the scene plan for final montage, not for literal subtitle counting.

A long-form documentary should usually target an editorially manageable scene count rather than maximizing scene granularity. A rough target band such as 260-280 scenes can be healthier than 450+ when pacing still reads well.
Assign an explicit generation preset per scene when possible, such as 4, 6, or 8 seconds, instead of leaving duration interpretation implicit.
Preserve one coherent documentary world with recurring characters, wardrobe, objects, and props when the story benefits from continuity.
Use richer shot-role taxonomies than a handful of overly broad buckets. Different story chapters should have distinct visual languages.
A prompt must show the concrete mechanism described by the narration, not merely a generic summary of the broader topic.
Avoid exact prompt duplication, especially in consecutive scenes. If two neighboring scenes cover related meaning, vary framing, action, scale, consequence, or point of view.
Use real brand context in semantic planning when the script is explicitly about real brands, while still avoiding readable logos and on-screen text inside the frame.

Store per-scene metadata that supports automation: source SRT linkage, timecodes, duration, duration preset, shot role, visual goal, brand context, continuity anchor, prompt, negative prompt, and audio policy.

key_capabilities: Supports direct ordering of image outputs as 001.png ... NNN.png.
Supports multiple reference images in one API request.
In this workflow, assume up to 10 reference images can be used in one prompt when needed.
important_rules: Prefer Fast Gen for production image generation rather than improvised local generation.
Generate the correct total number of shots after the max-5-second split logic is done.
Do not rely on later montage tricks to hide under-generated image counts.
Before each new submit, re-check whether the target mp4 already exists in veononstop_run/videos.
Use the API `duration` field explicitly for 4-second and 6-second renders. Omit it only when an 8-second render is desired by default behavior.
When the service returns cookie slot saturation, treat it as a capacity/backoff issue, not a content problem in the frame.
When the user explicitly asks to stop after 5 errors, count any 5 error events in a row and stop immediately.
Logs must be returned to the user after such a stop.
veononstop_video_pipeline.known_limitation: The service may spend a long time without producing useful output because the bottleneck is remote capacity and anti-abuse controls, not the local machine.

rules: The timeline is the source of truth for shot order, start/end times, and asset linkage.
Build sub-timelines for special generation campaigns instead of manually guessing shot indices.
For custom stride campaigns, generate dedicated timeline files.
Do not use zooms or reframing unless explicitly requested.
For mixed cuts, render each shot into a normalized short clip first, then concatenate clips and add audio.
Do not manually splice random files from the videos folder; always build from a manifest.
For partial deliveries, cut audio to the end time of the last included shot.

editorial_review_checklist.purpose: Use this checklist when refining veononstop videos so editorial decisions remain understandable to the viewer, not only technically correct to the editor.
storytelling_and_meaning: The video's core idea must be expressible in one sentence.
Every clip, scene, insert, and motion choice must serve the story or communicate information.
Remove fragments that repeat the same point, do not advance the story, or distract from the main narrative line.
The story should have a clear arc such as setup, development, escalation, and resolution.
At any moment, there should be a clear answer to the question: why is this part necessary?
narrative_and_retention: Within the first 15 seconds, the viewer should understand the context and why it is worth continuing.
At higher playback speed, the video must remain legible and not become confusing.
Include at least one genuine hook that creates a reason to keep watching.
Avoid stretches where nothing changes emotionally, informationally, or visually.
final_pass: The video without sound must still reveal a clear structure that can be followed visually.
Check the result on multiple devices and confirm that visuals and phone-speaker audio still read well.
Whenever possible, have someone unfamiliar with the project watch the final cut and verify they understand it without extra explanation.
editorial_review_checklist.judgment_rule: Not every video must satisfy every item literally. The checklist exists to force deliberate editorial choices and to optimize for viewer comprehension rather than editing-software convenience.

known_good_practical_preferences.vps_note: A VPS is useful later for unattended long renders and automation, but it does not solve veononstop service-side limits.
known_good_practical_preferences.render_hardware_note: CPU and NVMe matter for local ffmpeg montage. External AI video generation speed is mostly service-side.
known_good_practical_preferences.execution_note: For long unattended jobs, use append-only logs and stable manifests.
known_good_practical_preferences.reliability_note: When a service is unstable, prefer smaller, explicitly scoped sub-timelines over full brute-force sweeps.

anti_patterns_to_avoid: Do not derive final image counts from sentence counts alone.
Do not trust run_summary.json as historical memory.
Do not mix old generation campaigns and new target plans without a dedicated manifest.
Do not assume that a powerful local machine will materially improve veononstop throughput.
Do not attach all references to all prompts.
